prompt: A school survey records four things about each student. Which one is a QUANTITATIVE variable?

choices.label: Jersey number on the soccer team

hint: Quantitative means the numbers MEASURE or COUNT something, so averaging them makes sense.

hints.text: Quantitative means the numbers MEASURE or COUNT something, so averaging them makes sense.
A zip code and a jersey number are made of digits, but an "average zip code" is meaningless. They are labels.
Number of siblings is a count. An average of $1.8$ siblings makes sense, so it is quantitative: choice D.

explanation: A categorical variable sorts people into groups: lunch item, zip code and jersey number all do that, even when they use digits.
A quantitative variable counts or measures something, and arithmetic on it means something.
Number of siblings is a count, so it is quantitative. Choice D.

alternativeExplanations.title: The averaging test
steps: Ask: would an average of this variable mean anything?
Average zip code 94582.3? No. Average jersey number 11.4? No. Average favorite lunch? No.
Average number of siblings 1.8? Yes. That one is quantitative.
